citation: Anscombe, F. J. (1973), Graphs in Statistical Analysis, The American Statistician 27(1), 17-21, DOI 10.1080/00031305.1973.10478966 -- the eleven (x, y) pairs of data set 1, read from the unnumbered table on p. 19 captioned 'Four data sets, each comprising 11 (x, y) pairs'.
notes: The x column is printed once in the source and shared by data sets 1 to 3; the y column here is the one headed '1'. The row order is the order the table prints. THE INDEX IS A SPECIFICATION, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION: the source numbers its rows 1 to 11 and prints no other label, so the index is declared as a range starting at 1 and the eleven integers are produced by the builder rather than copied into this file. `dtype` is float because the table prints x to no decimal places and y to two; reading x as an integer would make the two columns disagree about what a value of this table is. WHAT THIS DATASET IS FOR AND WHAT IT IS NOT: Anscombe's point is that his four sets share every regression summary, so these pairs are evidence about transport and shape and never about estimation. A case that used them to check a fitted coefficient would be claiming something the source deliberately does not support.
